# Muse Douyin data and download tools

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

`douyin_download` accepts a selected official HTTPS video/share `url`, or a checked `urls` list, and writes verified media into the initiating session's `source/media/douyin/` directory. Public requests always ignore saved browser settings. `publicOnly:true` disables the internal-browser fallback. No browser profile, Cookie file, remembered account or arbitrary output directory is accepted by the tool.

## Runtime and configuration

The packaged integration requires Desktop Host protocol 6 and `douyinBrowser.version === 4` for page data and internal-browser acquisition. Versions 2 and 3 are rejected before browser data or download IPC. The version 4 download method requires the explicit fifth `nativeTimeoutMs` argument; application and plugin must be upgraded together. Installing the plugin alone does not add the browser transport. Desktop selects its validated bundled Python automatically, preserves explicit media executables, and discovers existing ffmpeg/ffprobe from the bundled media directory or ordinary PATH without installing packages or changing PATH. Mac installers include architecture-matched media executables; runtime discovery does not install dependencies. Packaged Python scripts and their extractor archive reside outside ASAR so the bundled interpreter can open them.

The public runner requires `agents`, `tools` and `subprocess`; browser fallback additionally uses the Host-owned transport. Deployment settings remain `pythonExecutable`, `ffprobeExecutable`, `ffmpegExecutable`, `settingsHome`, `requestTimeoutMs`, `timeoutMs`, `nativeTimeoutMs`, `maxDownloadBytes`, `graceMs`, `maxVideos`, `dataTimeoutMs`, and `maxComments`. Runner defaults are 120 seconds, 512 MiB and 20 links; page-data defaults are 30 seconds per link and 20 comments per page. `requestTimeoutMs` also allows delivery of the page result before the outer transport deadline. `maxDownloadBytes` (1 byte to 8 GiB) applies to public acquisition, internal-browser transfer and native-file verification. Internal-browser acquisition allows one active task. Preparation has a separate 120-second deadline; `nativeTimeoutMs` defaults to 30 minutes (integer 1 second to 2 hours) after media selection for the native transfer, then starts a fresh equal budget for complete local verification. Media association has its own 120-second deadline. The Host download IPC allows that association interval, the native budget and another 10 seconds for result delivery. This setting is independent of the public Python `timeoutMs`; tool deadlines include both acquisition paths, verification and transport cleanup. Configurations whose combined batch deadline exceeds the Node timer range are rejected; reduce `maxVideos` or the budgets. Missing verification executables return a blocked result.

## Page data and optional downloads

`douyin_data` accepts either `url` or `urls`, within `maxVideos`, and reads each selected work in order. `source` is `public`, `creator`, or `auto`; every successful result identifies `public-page` or `creator-page` and its observation time. Creator data requires normal login and evidence associating the exact work with that account. A browser login does not grant OAuth API scopes. `auto` uses the public page. `creator` opens the normal Creator content-management page and requires a matching string work ID, its aligned modification permission and the same ID in its statistics. It reads only the selected row; a missing verified own-work association returns `CREATOR_OWNERSHIP_UNVERIFIED`. Complete normal page loading or navigate to older works when needed. Public data does not substitute for unavailable creator data.

The five counters are plays, likes, comments, shares and favorites. Each counter reports an exact number, a rounded display, or `null` with a reason. Public counters come from the exact normal page detail response, its initial data, or the unique visible work action strip; exposed positive play counts are retained; missing values and placeholder zero remain unavailable. `includeComments:true` requests one observed page, bounded by `commentLimit` and `maxComments`; `commentCursor` applies to one selected link only. The total comment count is independent of returned comment items. The Desktop provider returns `COMMENTS_UNAVAILABLE` for comment content and pagination; it preserves observed counters and marks the result partial. The data format supports bounded comment text, comment IDs and numeric counts without account identifiers or credentials.

`download:true` acquires each selected work through the existing downloader, using its validated canonical URL when page data already resolved a share link and includes a separate download result. A failed download preserves available data; unavailable data can accompany a verified download. Batch results are `complete`, `partial` or `blocked`, with each item kept in input order. Cancellation joins the admitted browser read or child process, retains already observed data in the logged cancellation result and prevents the next link from starting. Page reads need no Python or media executables. Data remains in the model-visible, persisted tool result; this tool does not create another statistics file.

## Internal playback and results

After a public access failure, MUSE opens the official page in the existing isolated Browser panel for the currently selected Session. The user performs ordinary login, verification and playback. The initiating tool call starts the exact video download automatically after the initial main-document navigation finishes; playback inspection also waits for main-document loading to finish. Page-data observation waits for that initial document to finish before one target-bound reload; replacing the document during observation remains blocked. Failed playback inspection, DNS resolution, staging and native download initiation return separate blocked codes. Official Douyin video and Creator tabs retain login per workspace across application restarts; unrelated browser tabs use process-local storage. The downloader does not access external browser databases, export session credentials, manufacture signatures or bypass access controls, CAPTCHA or DRM.

The transport identifies media through `player-exact`, `provider-detail-verified`, or `player-metadata-verified`. `player-exact` pairs target-specific public `_ROUTER_DATA` or bounded player-parent `awemeInfo` properties with the exact visible player's observed successful MP4 source. A player-added `__vid` must equal the string work ID; other URL components and ordered decoded query entries must match the supplied address. Its native transfer retains the unchanged visible source. The current document retains at most 16 successful MP4 media or XHR response addresses and clears them on document replacement.

`provider-detail-verified` uses a page-generated official target detail JSON response, its exact work ID and bounded plain MP4 addresses, with matching visible-player duration. `player-metadata-verified` uses only the nearest player-parent public `awemeInfo`, requiring the exact string work ID and unique duration, dimensions and source facts. Repeated identical records are deduplicated; conflicting nearest records cannot be resolved by an outer recommendation roster. The metadata duration must match the visible player within 0.25 seconds and its aspect ratio within 1%. Metadata acquisition needs neither a prior MP4 response nor a detail response. Both verified branches permit loaded same-origin blob playback, report `currentSrcMatched:false`, and retain the unchanged plain HTTPS MP4 address from their respective source. Their receipts identify either official detail-response facts or `player-parent-awemeInfo` facts; one cannot stand in for the other. Acquisition never rewrites signed URLs, makes an API request, starts playback or changes a paused player.

CDN requests and redirects require public DNS results from the leased browser network context. A native verified transfer requires MP4 MIME and a successful final 200/206 response. Missing associations wait for available detail observation until the existing deadline; unavailable observation, protected media, fragments and ambiguous associations remain blocked. Public player addresses accept strings or `{src}` entries; acquisition requires a unique visible player with loaded media data and no media keys or active protection flags. Observation of 200/206 alone does not indicate a complete download. A one-use Host/owner/Session/task/lease/target authorization enables only the exact native attempt; generic browser downloads remain rejected. Session switching, document replacement, page closure, expiry, cancellation and Host disconnect revoke it and cancel verification.

Success requires actual nonzero bytes within the bound, ffprobe video/duration/dimension checks, complete ffmpeg decoding and SHA-256. Files selected from detail or player metadata must also match their source duration (within 0.25 seconds) and aspect ratio (within 1%). A source receipt includes the public video page, task/target IDs, bytes, duration, dimensions, identification method, a media hostname and hashed transient URL; it never includes Cookie, Authorization or signed media URLs. Files are published without overwriting existing output. `STAGED` is transport completion only, not the tool's downloaded result. Batches return `complete`, `partial` or `blocked` per verified item.

## Validation and packaging

Run `node --test tests/*.test.js` and `node scripts/pack.mjs --out /absolute/output/directory`. The tarball includes the canonical locked public Python extractor, but depends on the matching Host patch for internal-browser acquisition. The keyless page-data fixture uses authored counts and transport results; it does not establish live public or creator availability. The [blocked-batch Session replay](../../../snapshots/session/muse-douyin-blocked-batch/snapshot.yml) exercises the real tool and agent loop with isolated acquisition failures and preserves per-item diagnostics. Offline and synthetic media tests do not establish that the live acceptance URL can download. Live acceptance requires normal playback and a file-backed verified receipt for that URL.
